# Fields and what they do in Ziti

Every setting of every kind, with the field of the Ziti Edge Management API
it ends up in. The page of a kind has the same table with types and
defaults, an example and how the kind behaves.

## Service

Service; see [Service](resources/service.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the service. |
| `configs` | `configs`, as IDs | Configs are the names or IDs of the configs of the service, one per config type: what the tunnelers of clients intercept (intercept.v1) and where the tunnelers of hosts send the traffic (host.v1 or host.v2). Names are resolved to IDs. |
| `encryptionRequired` | `encryptionRequired` | EncryptionRequired makes the clients and the hosts of the service encrypt its traffic end to end, on top of the encryption between routers. |
| `maxIdleTimeMillis` | `maxIdleTimeMillis` | MaxIdleTimeMillis closes a circuit of the service that carried no traffic for so many milliseconds. Zero keeps idle circuits open. |
| `roleAttributes` | `roleAttributes` | RoleAttributes are the attributes policies select the service by, as "#attribute". |
| `tags` | `tags` | Tags are free-form labels Ziti stores with the service. They do not affect access or routing. |
| `terminatorStrategy` | `terminatorStrategy` | TerminatorStrategy says which of the terminators that host the service gets a new connection: smartrouting takes the one with the cheapest route, weighted and random spread the connections, sticky chooses like smartrouting and keeps a client on the terminator it got first while that terminator is available. One of `smartrouting`, `weighted`, `random`, `sticky`. |

## ConfigInterceptV1

Config of type `intercept.v1`; see [ConfigInterceptV1](resources/configinterceptv1.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the config. |
| `addresses` | `data.addresses` | Addresses are the host names, IP addresses and CIDR ranges the tunnelers of clients intercept. A name that starts with "*." stands for a whole domain. |
| `portRanges` | `data.portRanges` | PortRanges are the ports the tunnelers of clients intercept. |
| `portRanges[].high` | `data.portRanges[].high` | High is the last port of the range. |
| `portRanges[].low` | `data.portRanges[].low` | Low is the first port of the range. |
| `protocols` | `data.protocols` | Protocols the tunnelers of clients intercept: tcp, udp. |
| `dialOptions` | `data.dialOptions` | DialOptions say how the tunnelers of clients dial the service. |
| `dialOptions.connectTimeoutSeconds` | `data.dialOptions.connectTimeoutSeconds` | ConnectTimeoutSeconds is how long the tunneler of a client waits for the service to accept a connection. |
| `dialOptions.identity` | `data.dialOptions.identity` | Identity is the name of the hosting identity to dial, for a service whose hosts set listenOptions.bindUsingEdgeIdentity. |
| `sourceIp` | `data.sourceIp` | SourceIP is the address the hosting tunneler connects from, for a destination that must see where the client is. The host config of the service must allow it in allowedSourceAddresses. |
| `tags` | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

## ConfigHostV1

Config of type `host.v1`; see [ConfigHostV1](resources/confighostv1.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the config. |
| `address` | `data.address` | Address is the host name or IP address the hosting tunneler connects to. Leave it out when forwardAddress is set. |
| `allowedAddresses` | `data.allowedAddresses` | AllowedAddresses are the IP addresses, CIDR ranges and host names forwardAddress may connect to. |
| `allowedPortRanges` | `data.allowedPortRanges` | AllowedPortRanges are the ports forwardPort may connect to. |
| `allowedPortRanges[].high` | `data.allowedPortRanges[].high` | High is the last port of the range. |
| `allowedPortRanges[].low` | `data.allowedPortRanges[].low` | Low is the first port of the range. |
| `allowedProtocols` | `data.allowedProtocols` | AllowedProtocols are the protocols forwardProtocol may connect with: tcp, udp. |
| `allowedSourceAddresses` | `data.allowedSourceAddresses` | AllowedSourceAddresses are the addresses the hosting tunneler may connect from when the intercept config of the service sets sourceIp. |
| `forwardAddress` | `data.forwardAddress` | ForwardAddress connects to the address the client asked for, if allowedAddresses has it. |
| `forwardAddressTranslations` | `data.forwardAddressTranslations` | ForwardAddressTranslations move the address the client asked for into another range before the hosting tunneler connects. They apply when forwardAddress is true. |
| `forwardAddressTranslations[].from` | `data.forwardAddressTranslations[].from` | From is the first address of the range clients ask for, as a single IPv4 or IPv6 address without a prefix length, such as 10.0.0.0. Ziti refuses CIDR notation here: prefixLength gives the size of the range. |
| `forwardAddressTranslations[].prefixLength` | `data.forwardAddressTranslations[].prefixLength` | PrefixLength is the length of the prefix of from that is replaced by the prefix of to: the bits after it are kept. At most 32 for IPv4 and 128 for IPv6. From 0 to 128. |
| `forwardAddressTranslations[].to` | `data.forwardAddressTranslations[].to` | To is the first address of the range the hosting tunneler connects to instead, as a single address of the same family as from, such as 192.168.0.0. |
| `forwardPort` | `data.forwardPort` | ForwardPort connects to the port the client asked for, if allowedPortRanges has it. |
| `forwardProtocol` | `data.forwardProtocol` | ForwardProtocol connects with the protocol the client used, if allowedProtocols has it. |
| `httpChecks` | `data.httpChecks` | HTTPChecks are health checks the hosting tunneler makes with HTTP requests. Their actions change how its terminator is offered. |
| `httpChecks[].actions` | `data.httpChecks[].actions` | Actions to take on the results of the check. |
| `httpChecks[].actions[].action` | `data.httpChecks[].actions[].action` | Action to take: "mark unhealthy" stops offering the terminator, "mark healthy" offers it again, "increase cost N" and "decrease cost N" change its cost, "send event" reports the result to the controller. |
| `httpChecks[].actions[].duration` | `data.httpChecks[].actions[].duration` | Duration is how long the results must have lasted before the action runs, as a duration such as 30s. |
| `httpChecks[].actions[].trigger` | `data.httpChecks[].actions[].trigger` | Trigger says which results run the action: checks that pass, checks that fail, or a change from one to the other. One of `pass`, `fail`, `change`. |
| `httpChecks[].actions[].consecutiveEvents` | `data.httpChecks[].actions[].consecutiveEvents` | ConsecutiveEvents is how many results in a row it takes before the action runs. |
| `httpChecks[].interval` | `data.httpChecks[].interval` | Interval between two checks, as a duration such as 10s. |
| `httpChecks[].method` | `data.httpChecks[].method` | Method of the request: GET, PUT, POST or PATCH. One of `GET`, `PUT`, `POST`, `PATCH`. |
| `httpChecks[].timeout` | `data.httpChecks[].timeout` | Timeout after which a check without an answer fails, as a duration such as 5s. |
| `httpChecks[].url` | `data.httpChecks[].url` | URL the hosting tunneler requests. |
| `httpChecks[].body` | `data.httpChecks[].body` | Body of the request. |
| `httpChecks[].expectInBody` | `data.httpChecks[].expectInBody` | ExpectInBody is text the response of a check that passes contains. |
| `httpChecks[].expectStatus` | `data.httpChecks[].expectStatus` | ExpectStatus is the status code of a check that passes. From 100 to 599. |
| `listenOptions` | `data.listenOptions` | ListenOptions say how the hosting tunneler offers the service to the network. |
| `listenOptions.bindUsingEdgeIdentity` | `data.listenOptions.bindUsingEdgeIdentity` | BindUsingEdgeIdentity offers the service under the name of the hosting identity, so that a client can dial one host among several. |
| `listenOptions.connectTimeout` | `data.listenOptions.connectTimeout` | ConnectTimeout is how long the hosting tunneler waits for the destination to accept a connection, as a duration such as 5s. |
| `listenOptions.cost` | `data.listenOptions.cost` | Cost of the terminator: Ziti prefers cheaper terminators. From 0 to 65535. |
| `listenOptions.maxConnections` | `data.listenOptions.maxConnections` | MaxConnections is the number of connections to edge routers the hosting tunneler listens for the service on. From 1 to 65535. |
| `listenOptions.precedence` | `data.listenOptions.precedence` | Precedence of the terminator: one with required is used before one with default, and one with failed only when nothing else is left. One of `default`, `required`, `failed`. |
| `port` | `data.port` | Port the hosting tunneler connects to. Leave it out when forwardPort is set. From 1 to 65535. |
| `portChecks` | `data.portChecks` | PortChecks are health checks the hosting tunneler makes by opening a TCP connection. Their actions change how its terminator is offered. |
| `portChecks[].actions` | `data.portChecks[].actions` | Actions to take on the results of the check. |
| `portChecks[].actions[].action` | `data.portChecks[].actions[].action` | Action to take: "mark unhealthy" stops offering the terminator, "mark healthy" offers it again, "increase cost N" and "decrease cost N" change its cost, "send event" reports the result to the controller. |
| `portChecks[].actions[].duration` | `data.portChecks[].actions[].duration` | Duration is how long the results must have lasted before the action runs, as a duration such as 30s. |
| `portChecks[].actions[].trigger` | `data.portChecks[].actions[].trigger` | Trigger says which results run the action: checks that pass, checks that fail, or a change from one to the other. One of `pass`, `fail`, `change`. |
| `portChecks[].actions[].consecutiveEvents` | `data.portChecks[].actions[].consecutiveEvents` | ConsecutiveEvents is how many results in a row it takes before the action runs. |
| `portChecks[].address` | `data.portChecks[].address` | Address the hosting tunneler connects to, as host:port. |
| `portChecks[].interval` | `data.portChecks[].interval` | Interval between two checks, as a duration such as 10s. |
| `portChecks[].timeout` | `data.portChecks[].timeout` | Timeout after which a check without an answer fails, as a duration such as 5s. |
| `protocol` | `data.protocol` | Protocol the hosting tunneler connects with: tcp or udp. Leave it out when forwardProtocol is set. One of `tcp`, `udp`. |
| `proxy` | `data.proxy` | Proxy makes the hosting tunneler connect through a proxy. |
| `proxy.address` | `data.proxy.address` | Address of the proxy, as host:port. |
| `proxy.type` | `data.proxy.type` | Type of the proxy. Ziti knows http. One of `http`. |
| `tags` | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

## ServicePolicy

Service policy; see [ServicePolicy](resources/servicepolicy.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the policy. |
| `type` | `type` | Type says what the policy grants: Dial lets the identities connect to the services, Bind lets them host the services. One of `Dial`, `Bind`. |
| `identityRoles` | `identityRoles`; `@name` is sent as `@id` | IdentityRoles is a list of identity role selectors: "#all", "#attribute" or "@name", where name is the name or the ID of an identity. Names are resolved to IDs. |
| `postureCheckRoles` | `postureCheckRoles`; `@name` is sent as `@id` | PostureCheckRoles is a list of posture check role selectors: "#all", "#attribute" or "@name", where name is the name or the ID of a posture check. Names are resolved to IDs. |
| `semantic` | `semantic` | Semantic says how the "#attribute" selectors of one list combine: AnyOf selects what has any of the attributes, AllOf what has all of them. One of `AnyOf`, `AllOf`. |
| `serviceRoles` | `serviceRoles`; `@name` is sent as `@id` | ServiceRoles is a list of service role selectors: "#all", "#attribute" or "@name", where name is the name or the ID of a service. Names are resolved to IDs. |
| `tags` | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

## Identity

Identity that enrolls with a one-time token; see [Identity](resources/identity.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the identity. |
| `appData` | `appData` | AppData is a map of data for the applications that use the identity. |
| `authPolicyId` | `authPolicyId`, as an ID | AuthPolicyID is the name or ID of the auth policy that governs how the identity authenticates. Ziti assigns its default auth policy when this is not set. |
| `defaultHostingCost` | `defaultHostingCost` | DefaultHostingCost is the cost of the terminators the identity hosts. From 0 to 65535. |
| `defaultHostingPrecedence` | `defaultHostingPrecedence` | DefaultHostingPrecedence is the precedence of the terminators the identity hosts. One of `default`, `required`, `failed`. |
| `enrollmentDuration` | `expiresAt` of the enrollment that replaces one that expired or is gone | EnrollmentDuration is how long an enrollment token is valid that replaces one that expired or is gone, 180m when this is not set. It does not apply to the first token, which is valid for as long as the Ziti controller is configured to make it, and an identity without an enrollment has no use for it. Rule: enrollmentDuration must be at least 5m. |
| `externalId` | `externalId` | ExternalID identifies the identity to an external JWT signer. |
| `isAdmin` | `isAdmin` | IsAdmin grants admin privileges to the identity. |
| `roleAttributes` | `roleAttributes` | RoleAttributes are the attributes policies select the identity by, as "#attribute". |
| `serviceHostingCosts` | `serviceHostingCosts`, keyed by service ID | ServiceHostingCosts overrides the hosting cost per service. Keys are service names or IDs. |
| `serviceHostingPrecedences` | `serviceHostingPrecedences`, keyed by service ID | ServiceHostingPrecedences overrides the hosting precedence (default, required, failed) per service. Keys are service names or IDs. |
| `tags` | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |
| `type` | `type` | Type of the identity. It cannot be changed after creation. One of `Default`, `User`, `Device`, `Service`. |

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the identity. |
| `updbUsername` | `enrollment.updb` | UpdbUsername is the username the identity authenticates with. It cannot be changed after creation. |
| `appData` | `appData` | AppData is a map of data for the applications that use the identity. |
| `authPolicyId` | `authPolicyId`, as an ID | AuthPolicyID is the name or ID of the auth policy that governs how the identity authenticates. Ziti assigns its default auth policy when this is not set. |
| `defaultHostingCost` | `defaultHostingCost` | DefaultHostingCost is the cost of the terminators the identity hosts. From 0 to 65535. |
| `defaultHostingPrecedence` | `defaultHostingPrecedence` | DefaultHostingPrecedence is the precedence of the terminators the identity hosts. One of `default`, `required`, `failed`. |
| `enrollmentDuration` | `expiresAt` of the enrollment that replaces one that expired or is gone | EnrollmentDuration is how long an enrollment token is valid that replaces one that expired or is gone, 180m when this is not set. It does not apply to the first token, which is valid for as long as the Ziti controller is configured to make it, and an identity without an enrollment has no use for it. Rule: enrollmentDuration must be at least 5m. |
| `externalId` | `externalId` | ExternalID identifies the identity to an external JWT signer. |
| `isAdmin` | `isAdmin` | IsAdmin grants admin privileges to the identity. |
| `roleAttributes` | `roleAttributes` | RoleAttributes are the attributes policies select the identity by, as "#attribute". |
| `serviceHostingCosts` | `serviceHostingCosts`, keyed by service ID | ServiceHostingCosts overrides the hosting cost per service. Keys are service names or IDs. |
| `serviceHostingPrecedences` | `serviceHostingPrecedences`, keyed by service ID | ServiceHostingPrecedences overrides the hosting precedence (default, required, failed) per service. Keys are service names or IDs. |
| `tags` | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |
| `type` | `type` | Type of the identity. It cannot be changed after creation. One of `Default`, `User`, `Device`, `Service`. |

## EdgeRouter

Edge router; see [EdgeRouter](resources/edgerouter.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the edge router. |
| `cost` | `cost` | Cost of a route through the router: Ziti prefers cheaper routes. |
| `isTunnelerEnabled` | `isTunnelerEnabled` | IsTunnelerEnabled lets the router intercept and host services itself, like a tunneler. Ziti creates an identity with the name of the router for that. |

## AuthPolicy

Auth policy; see [AuthPolicy](resources/authpolicy.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the auth policy. |
| `primary` | `primary` | Primary authentication methods. A method that is not set is not allowed. |
| `primary.cert` | `primary.cert` | Cert-based authentication. |
| `primary.cert.allowExpiredCerts` | `primary.cert.allowExpiredCerts` | AllowExpiredCerts allows expired certificates. |
| `primary.cert.allowed` | `primary.cert.allowed` | Allowed enables cert authentication. |
| `primary.extJwt` | `primary.extJwt` | External JWT authentication. |
| `primary.extJwt.allowed` | `primary.extJwt.allowed` | Allowed enables external JWT authentication. |
| `primary.extJwt.allowedSigners` | `primary.extJwt.allowedSigners`, as IDs | AllowedSigners is the list of names or IDs of the external JWT signers whose tokens are accepted. Every signer is accepted if it is empty. |
| `primary.updb` | `primary.updb` | Password (UPDB) authentication. |
| `primary.updb.allowed` | `primary.updb.allowed` | Allowed enables password authentication. |
| `primary.updb.lockoutDurationMinutes` | `primary.updb.lockoutDurationMinutes` | LockoutDurationMinutes is the duration of a lockout in minutes. Zero locks the identity until an administrator unlocks it. |
| `primary.updb.maxAttempts` | `primary.updb.maxAttempts` | MaxAttempts is the number of failed logins before lockout. |
| `primary.updb.minPasswordLength` | `primary.updb.minPasswordLength` | MinPasswordLength is the minimum password length. |
| `primary.updb.requireMixedCase` | `primary.updb.requireMixedCase` | RequireMixedCase requires passwords to have upper and lower case letters. |
| `primary.updb.requireNumberChar` | `primary.updb.requireNumberChar` | RequireNumberChar requires passwords to have a digit. |
| `primary.updb.requireSpecialChar` | `primary.updb.requireSpecialChar` | RequireSpecialChar requires passwords to have a special character. |
| `secondary` | `secondary` | Secondary authentication factors. |
| `secondary.requireExtJwtSigner` | `secondary.requireExtJwtSigner`, as an ID | RequireExtJWTSigner is the name or ID of an external JWT signer whose token is required in addition to the primary method. |
| `secondary.requireTotp` | `secondary.requireTotp` | RequireTOTP requires a time-based one-time password. |
| `tags` | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

## ExternalJWTSigner

External JWT signer; see [ExternalJWTSigner](resources/externaljwtsigner.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the external JWT signer. |
| `audience` | `audience` | Audience is the aud claim a token must have to be accepted. |
| `issuer` | `issuer` | Issuer is the iss claim of the tokens of this signer. No two signers may have the same issuer. |
| `certPem` | `certPem` | CertPem is the PEM encoded certificate that verifies the tokens of the signer, for a signer without a JSON Web Key Set. |
| `claimsProperty` | `claimsProperty` | ClaimsProperty is the claim of a token that tells which identity it is for. Ziti takes the subject if it is not set. |
| `clientId` | `clientId` | ClientID is the OAuth client ID clients obtain a token with. |
| `enabled` | `enabled` | Enabled makes Ziti accept the tokens of this signer. |
| `enrollAttributeClaimsSelector` | `enrollAttributeClaimsSelector` | EnrollAttributeClaimsSelector is the claim of a token that holds the role attributes of the identity an enrollment creates. |
| `enrollAuthPolicyId` | `enrollAuthPolicyId`, as an ID | EnrollAuthPolicyID is the name or ID of the auth policy of the identities an enrollment creates. Ziti takes the default auth policy if it is not set. |
| `enrollNameClaimsSelector` | `enrollNameClaimsSelector` | EnrollNameClaimsSelector is the claim of a token that names the identity an enrollment creates. Ziti takes the subject if it is not set. |
| `enrollToCertEnabled` | `enrollToCertEnabled` | EnrollToCertEnabled lets the holder of a token of this signer enroll, which creates an identity that authenticates with a certificate. |
| `enrollToTokenEnabled` | `enrollToTokenEnabled` | EnrollToTokenEnabled lets the holder of a token of this signer enroll, which creates an identity that authenticates with tokens of this signer. |
| `externalAuthUrl` | `externalAuthUrl` | ExternalAuthURL is the URL clients obtain a token of this signer from. |
| `jwksEndpoint` | `jwksEndpoint` | JwksEndpoint is the URL of the JSON Web Key Set of the signer. It must name a host, and its scheme must be http or https, in any case. Must match `^[Hh][Tt][Tt][Pp][Ss]?://([^/?#@]*@)?(\[[0-9A-Fa-f:.]+\]\|[^/?#@:\[\]]+)(:[0-9]*)?([/?#].*)?$`. |
| `kid` | `kid` | Kid is the key ID of the certificate in certPem: the kid header of the tokens it verifies. |
| `scopes` | `scopes` | Scopes are the OAuth scopes clients request a token with. |
| `tags` | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |
| `targetToken` | `targetToken` | TargetToken is the token clients present to Ziti: the access token or the ID token. One of `ACCESS`, `ID`. |
| `useExternalId` | `useExternalId` | UseExternalID looks the identity up by its externalId instead of its ID. |

## CertificateAuthority

Third-party certificate authority; see [CertificateAuthority](resources/certificateauthority.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the certificate authority. |
| `certPem` | `certPem` | CertPem is the PEM encoded certificate of the certificate authority. It must be a CA certificate that no other certificate authority in Ziti has, and it cannot be changed after creation. |
| `externalIdClaim` | `externalIdClaim` | ExternalIDClaim takes the external ID of an identity from its certificate. Without it, identities are recognized by the fingerprint of their certificate. Rule: the SCHEME matcher is for the SAN_URI location, which takes no PREFIX or SUFFIX matcher. Rule: matcherCriteria is required unless the matcher is ALL. Rule: parserCriteria is required for the SPLIT parser. |
| `externalIdClaim.index` | `externalIdClaim.index` | Index of the external ID to use among the ones found, starting at zero. At least 0. |
| `externalIdClaim.location` | `externalIdClaim.location` | Location of the values in the certificate: its common name, or the URIs or email addresses of its subject alternative names. One of `COMMON_NAME`, `SAN_URI`, `SAN_EMAIL`. |
| `externalIdClaim.matcher` | `externalIdClaim.matcher` | Matcher selects the values to consider: ALL of them, those with a PREFIX or a SUFFIX, or the URIs with a SCHEME. One of `ALL`, `PREFIX`, `SUFFIX`, `SCHEME`. |
| `externalIdClaim.matcherCriteria` | `externalIdClaim.matcherCriteria` | MatcherCriteria is the prefix, suffix or scheme the matcher looks for. |
| `externalIdClaim.parser` | `externalIdClaim.parser` | Parser turns a selected value into external IDs: NONE takes it as is, SPLIT splits it at a separator. One of `NONE`, `SPLIT`. |
| `externalIdClaim.parserCriteria` | `externalIdClaim.parserCriteria` | ParserCriteria is the separator of the SPLIT parser. |
| `identityNameFormat` | `identityNameFormat` | IdentityNameFormat is the name of the identities that automatic enrollment creates. It may contain [caName], [caId], [commonName], [requestedName] and [identityId]. |
| `identityRoles` | `identityRoles` | IdentityRoles are the role attributes of the identities that automatic enrollment creates. |
| `isAuthEnabled` | `isAuthEnabled` | IsAuthEnabled lets identities authenticate with a certificate of this certificate authority. |
| `isAutoCaEnrollmentEnabled` | `isAutoCaEnrollmentEnabled` | IsAutoCaEnrollmentEnabled lets anyone with a certificate of this certificate authority enroll, which creates an identity. |
| `isOttCaEnrollmentEnabled` | `isOttCaEnrollmentEnabled` | IsOttCaEnrollmentEnabled lets identities enroll with a one-time token and a certificate of this certificate authority. |
| `tags` | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

| `tags` | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

## PostureCheckProcess

Posture check of type `PROCESS`; see [PostureCheckProcess](resources/posturecheckprocess.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the posture check. |
| `process` | `process` | Process that must be running. |
| `process.osType` | `process.osType` | OsType is the operating system the process runs on. One of `Windows`, `WindowsServer`, `Android`, `iOS`, `Linux`, `macOS`. |
| `process.path` | `process.path` | Path of the executable. |
| `process.hashes` | `process.hashes` | Hashes are the SHA-512 hashes the executable may have. Any executable passes if there are none. Ziti keeps them as a set, so their order and duplicates do not matter. |
| `process.signerFingerprint` | `process.signerFingerprint` | SignerFingerprint is the SHA-1 fingerprint of the certificate the executable must be signed with. Must match `^([0-9A-Fa-f]+([ :.-][0-9A-Fa-f]+)*)?$`. |
| `roleAttributes` | `roleAttributes` | RoleAttributes are the attributes service policies select the posture check by, as "#attribute". |

## PostureCheckMultiProcess

Posture check of type `PROCESS_MULTI`; see [PostureCheckMultiProcess](resources/posturecheckmultiprocess.md).

| Field | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | `name` | Name of the posture check. |
| `processes` | `processes` | Processes to look for. Ziti identifies a process by its operating system and path, so each pair may be listed once, and their order does not matter. |
| `processes[].osType` | `processes[].osType` | OsType is the operating system the process runs on. One of `Windows`, `WindowsServer`, `Android`, `iOS`, `Linux`, `macOS`. |
| `processes[].path` | `processes[].path` | Path of the executable. |
| `processes[].hashes` | `processes[].hashes` | Hashes are the SHA-512 hashes the executable may have. Any executable passes if there are none. Ziti keeps them as a set, so their order and duplicates do not matter. |
| `processes[].signerFingerprints` | `processes[].signerFingerprints` | SignerFingerprints are the SHA-1 fingerprints of the certificates the executable may be signed with. Any signer passes if there are none. Ziti keeps them as a set, so their order and duplicates do not matter. |
| `roleAttributes` | `roleAttributes` | RoleAttributes are the attributes service policies select the posture check by, as "#attribute". |
| `semantic` | `semantic` | Semantic says whether all of the processes must be running (AllOf) or any one of them (AnyOf). One of `AllOf`, `AnyOf`. |
| `tags` | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |
